crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was thirteen and her mother left, her best friend read her letter aloud to the whole class so they'd be kind. After that, she answered everything with "I'm fine."
Every Sunday by the lounge fire, one prisoner read out the unsigned slips from her worry tin. "A worry said aloud weighs less." {WITCH_NAME} always sat beside her and never added one.

"Someone here has carried this alone too long," the girl said one Sunday, and read out {WITCH_NAME}'s first letter since that classroom. {WITCH_NAME} had touched it: only the girl could read it; everyone else saw a laundry list. The whole lounge turned to {WITCH_NAME}. She smiled at them. "I'm fine."
The next evening she asked the girl to the shower room at seven. "No one can hear in there. I'll tell you the rest. Only you."

Before seven, the girl pinned her usual slip to her barred cell door so no one would wonder: "Shower room. Back by eight." At seven, {WITCH_NAME} pressed a hand over the mouth that had read her letter aloud and held her down on the wet shower-room tiles until she was still.

At twenty past seven, walking to the lounge with {WITCH_NAME}, the girl's roommate read the slip: "Back by eight." At half past eight, prisoners fetching cardigans read "Back by ten." At half past nine they found the girl on the shower-room tiles. In the trial court, they decided she had come back after twenty past seven to change it and died while {WITCH_NAME} sat in the lounge.
The roommate read it again: still "Back by eight." Beside her, someone read "Back by ten."

Returning through the cell corridor, {WITCH_NAME} had touched the slip so only the roommate saw its real words. The prisoners understood: the slip had never changed. The girl had died before twenty past seven, when no one knew where {WITCH_NAME} was.
fields.epitaph: Her letter had one reader. Now it has none, and to every eye it says nothing at all.
fields.epithet: The Girl Who Is Always Fine
execution: A barred cell door as tall as the court rises on the execution stand, and she is chained upright with her back to its bars. Facing her is a brass slip pin as long as a spear. A paper slip hangs across her chest for every spectator to read: "I'm fine."
The pin drives through the slip over her heart and pins her to the bars like a notice.
She hangs still on the bars. To every eye, the slip still reads "I'm fine."

magic.name: For Your Eyes Only
magic.text: Any page she touches shows its real words only to readers she chooses; everyone else sees harmless, ordinary words.
